title: What is the ratio of the three parts of a hexagon?
description: A regular hexagon is cut from its centre into six equal triangles. The trapezium holds three of them, the rhombus two and the triangle one, so the three areas are in the ratio three to one to two, and together they make six.
teaching_notes: One idea: join the centre of a regular hexagon to its corners to get six equal triangles, then count the triangles in each part. Watch for students who say three parts must be in the ratio one to one to one.

source: A regular hexagon divided into a trapezium, an equilateral triangle and a rhombus, find the ratio of their areas
video_script.why: The child has cut a trapezium into pieces whose areas are known and now compares three parts of a hexagon by counting equal triangles.
video_script.substitution: The book question gives no lengths, so the parts are counted in equal triangles.
video_script.anchor: a regular hexagon divided into a trapezium, an equilateral triangle and a rhombus
video_script.payoff_line: The trapezium, the triangle and the rhombus are in the ratio three to one to two.
maths_rules: joining the centre of a regular hexagon to its six corners gives 6 equal equilateral triangles
the trapezium is half the hexagon: 3 of these triangles
the rhombus is 2 of these triangles and the equilateral triangle is 1
video_script.design: One regular hexagon stays all video. Lines from the centre to the corners cut it into six equal triangles, and each part is counted in triangles. The three parts are shaded in three colours.
open_questions: The figure is not in the book text. The split used is the usual one: the trapezium is half the hexagon, and the other half is a rhombus and a triangle.
